newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rates ease a little.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rates ease a little.

text.p: Dutch call money was somewhat lower on Thursday after coming under upward pressure for several days, but dealers said the rate could rise again on Friday when the central bank allocates new liquidity.
Later today, the Dutch central bank will announce a new special advances pact, under which it will allocate new liquidity on Friday.
Dealers said the special advances rate was expected to remain unchanged at 2.50 percent and several expected a seven-day pact.
Call money was bid at 2.75 percent versus 2.88 yesterday.
"But, some trades were done at 2.93 percent on Wednesday, so the upward pressure is less today," said one dealer.
Three-month deposits were unchanged at 2.90 percent bid.
The guilder was lingering near yesterday's close at 112.230 per 100 marks versus 112.235 on Wednesday.
